chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Ma'mar ibn Yahya and Isma'il from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He gives one salutation, whether he is an Imam or not.
So it is to be understood based on what we have previously mentioned, which is that when the follower has no one on his left, and that which also clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated.

key_terms.اَلْمَأْمُومُ: The follower (one who prays behind the Imam)
key_terms.تَسْلِيمَة: Salutation (the act of turning the head to the right and left at the end of prayer)

ai.seo_question: How many salutations should a follower give in prayer if there is no one on his left?
ai.summary: This narration from the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a follower offers a single salutation (taslim) regardless of whether he is following an Imam or praying individually, provided no one is positioned to his left. This ruling is contextualized within the broader jurisprudential discussion on the completeness of the follower's prayer, distinguishing it from cases where multiple salutations might be required to ensure the congregation's unity. The condition of having no one on the left side highlights the practical application of this rule in varying prayer configurations.
